$description: Project Settings › Deploy: where the site ships, and what it is built with. One row over `build.adapter`, and the sentence a failed write leaves behind. The adapter (`surfaces/settings-deploy.ts`) hands in the chosen adapter, the enumeration it is chosen from and whatever the last write had to say; the document draws them and hands the change straight back. Nothing here reads `project.json` — a section that re-read the config while drawing would be a second opinion about a file one module already owns.

style.$description: What is NOT in this block is most of the conversion. Four borrowed rules had nothing to transcribe: `.settings-field-label` and `.settings-field-desc` drew a row's label and the sentence under it, and `jx-field` draws both — with the label actually NAMING the control, which the bare `<label class=…>` beside the picker never did; `.settings-field` added a 20px bottom margin to separate one row from the next, and this section has one row, so the margin separated it from the end of the section; and `.settings-section` was never defined by any stylesheet at all, which is why it sits in `check-styles.ts`'s allow-list rather than in a rule.

& [part=\"error\"].$description: A write that failed, said under the section title rather than pinned to the picker: settings save on change, so a silent rejection would read as "my edit just vanished", and what failed was the whole file rather than the value. Its size read `--spectrum-font-size-75` with a 12px fallback, which resolved only inside `<sp-theme>` — a document is mounted in the settings pane, where that name is not in scope and the fallback is all it would ever have taken — so the size is the kit's scale and the colour is the studio layer's.

& [part=\"adapter\"].$description: How wide the picker may grow. A control offering five short words does not want the width of a 900px pane, and 320px is the one thing `.settings-build-adapter` said that the kit does not — the same measure the two pickers in Locales take.

$props.label: Platform Adapter
$props.description: What the site is built for. Static writes plain files; the others emit a server entry for that runtime.
